content.text: Congenital narrowing of the aortic lumen @ the dist or descending aorta
(70%), MV defects, patent ductus arteriosus, Turner syndrome

•narrowing of the aorta MC @ the insertion of the ductus arteriosus dist to the origin of the Lt subclavian v. results in HTN in the arteries prox to the lesion (ex, primary arteries supplying the UE) w/ relative hypotension in the LE
•over time, the body compensates by developing collaterals around the coarctation (ex, IC arteries)
•→ adults typically aSx d/t collateral growth
: narrowing occurs dist to the ductus arteriosum
: narrowing occurs prox to the ductus arteriosum
•Ductal: narrowing @ the insertion of the ductus arteriosus; appears when the ductus closes
May range from aSx to HF or shock after birth w/ closure of the patent ductus arteriosus
Systol BP in UE > than in LE
Continuous murmur in mid- to late systol, best @ midline upper back b/n scapulae or over Lt ant chest
(narrowed aorta looks like the notch of the # 3)
- balloon angioplasty w/ or w/o stent placement
- maintains a patent ductus arteriosus, reducing sxs & improves the LE blood flow
▪︎1 of the 4 parts of Tetralogy of Fallot (w/ RV outflow tract obstruction, RVH, overriding aorta)
▪︎holosystolic murmur (chart: VSDs, small muscular defects, regurg)
▪︎Sx at younger age → recurrent resp infections, failure to thrive, exertional dyspnea
▪︎PE: fixed split S2 (chart: abnl S2 in ASD/pulm HTN); murmur max intensity LUSB
▪︎ductus arteriosus stays patent (normal: closes → ligamentum arteriosum, its remnant)
▪︎continuous machinelike murmur best heard at pulmonic area w/ wide pulse pressures
▪︎4 parts: (1) RV outflow tract obstruction, (2) RV hypertrophy, (3) overriding aorta, (4) VSD
▪︎tet spells: cyanotic during episodes of crying, feeding, or agitation; worse w/ crying/feeding (d/t worsening pulm outflow obstruction)
▪︎assoc w/ coarctation (esp preductal = narrowing proximal to the ductus arteriosus; life-threatening if severe)
▪︎assoc also: bicuspid aortic valve, intracranial aneurysms
